# Patient RX System v2.0.69

## Security Hardening And FortiGate Proxy HTTPS Support

This release promotes the tested staging/development hardening work into production and adds proxy-aware HTTPS behavior for FortiGate SSL VPN deployments.

## What Changed

- Browser auth now uses the server-set `HttpOnly` `rxToken` cookie instead of browser-readable full-token storage.
- CSRF protection is enforced for cookie-authenticated unsafe API requests.
- System Settings rendering paths were hardened to reduce stored-XSS risk from settings/user values.
- SMTP passwords are encrypted at rest when saved through System Settings.
- Document upload UI/routes are removed, and Google Drive document upload API usage is disabled.
- FortiGate proxy handling now supports `Browser HTTPS -> FortiGate -> internal HTTP -> Node app` without redirecting to broken internal HTTPS.
- `.env.example` now documents the safe HTTPS/proxy flags.

## Database Impact

- No schema changes.
- No destructive data changes.
- Existing patients, RX records, workflow records, audit logs, reports, and settings are preserved.
- SMTP password values are encrypted when saved through System Settings after the update.
- Existing production documents are not expected for this deployment; document upload remains disabled.

## Validation Completed

- Tested on staging at `http://localhost:3100`.
- Confirmed FortiGate-style backend HTTP requests return `200 OK` and set `Secure; SameSite=None` cookies.
- Confirmed direct internal HTTPS to `192.168.15.87:3100` is not required because Node is not serving TLS directly.
- JavaScript and Node syntax checks passed for modified files.
- Staging config, security hardening, import guard, and service-date cycle context smoke checks passed.
- Production release build completed before tagging this release.

## Production Verification Checklist

After installing the `v2.0.69` update:

1. Confirm the sidebar/version badge or `/api/version` shows `2.0.69`.
2. Open the normal production FortiGate URL and confirm the browser address starts with `https://rx.camperos.net:10443`.
3. Confirm the FortiGate backend/bookmark uses internal protocol `HTTP`, host `192.168.15.87`, and the production app port.
4. Log in and confirm the browser cookie for `rxToken` is `HttpOnly`, `Secure`, and `SameSite=None` when accessed through FortiGate.
5. Confirm there is no redirect to `https://192.168.15.87:<port>`.
6. Add or edit a test patient and save successfully.
7. Open a patient/RX record and confirm document upload controls are not shown.
8. Open System Settings, save a harmless setting, and confirm the page still renders correctly.
9. If SMTP settings are used, send a test email from System Settings.
